purpose: Distinct user questions for the vLLM vs Ollama concurrency sweep. Each request uses a different question so a repeated prompt does not make prefix caching the main effect. Both engines receive the questions in this order.
questions: Why do ice cubes crack loudly when they are dropped into a glass of water that is already warm?
How does a compass needle settle on north when no magnet is touching the needle itself?
What makes a covered bowl of bread dough expand if the baker adds no baking powder at all?
Why does a metal bench feel colder than a wooden bench when both have sat outside all morning?
How can a ship made of steel float on a lake while a solid steel bolt dropped beside it sinks?
Why is the daytime sky usually blue overhead and often orange near the horizon at sunset?
How does a home thermostat decide the moment to turn a heater on and the moment to stop it?
Why do some party balloons look smaller the next morning even though the knot never came undone?
What causes the rumble of thunder to reach you later than the flash of lightning you already saw?
How does sunscreen reduce a sunburn without blocking every bit of daylight from touching the skin?
Why is a moving bicycle easier to balance than the same bicycle held still at a traffic light?
How can a tiny seed become a tall tree when nobody piles extra soil on top of the spot where it fell?
Why do wet clothes on a line dry faster on a windy afternoon than on a still afternoon?
What makes a rainbow visible only when the sun is behind you and rain is still falling in front of you?
How does a kitchen refrigerator keep food cold without leaving its door open to the room?
Why does a wide shallow bowl of soup cool faster than the same soup left in a tall narrow cup?
How can noise-cancelling headphones soften a steady engine hum yet still let you hear a sudden clap?
Why do many green leaves turn red or yellow in autumn even though the branches are still alive?
What keeps an orbiting satellite moving around Earth instead of dropping straight back to the ground?
How does a packet of yeast make pizza dough rise during the hour before the baker slides it into the oven?
Why is ocean water salty when the rain that fills the rivers flowing into it is not salty?
How can a magnifying glass char a dry leaf when the air around the leaf does not feel especially hot?
Why do passengers' ears pop during takeoff as the airplane climbs away from the airport?
What makes frost appear on a car windshield on a clear night when no rain fell after sunset?
How does a microwave oven warm a bowl of leftovers without setting the ceramic bowl on fire?
Why can a row of birds sit on a power line without each bird receiving an electric shock?
How does a heavy passenger airplane stay aloft once its wheels have left the runway?
Why does a cook add salt to a pot of water when the goal is to change how the water boils?
What causes a bathroom mirror to fog during a hot shower when the door and window are both shut?
How does a rooftop solar panel turn ordinary daylight into electricity that can charge a phone?
Why do some underripe fruits soften faster inside a closed paper bag than they do on an open plate?
How can a concrete dam on a river produce electricity from water that is only traveling downhill?
Why does a guitar string sound higher after the player shortens the part of the string that can vibrate?
What makes a rain cloud look white or gray from the ground while the raindrops falling from it are clear?
How does the right key open a pin lock when a key with a similar shape leaves the same lock shut?
Why do stars seem to twinkle on a clear night while a bright planet in the same sky usually looks steady?
How can a vacuum flask keep tea hot for hours when the flask itself stays cool enough to hold?
Why does a puddle on asphalt disappear on a sunny day even though the water never reached a boil?
What makes a tuning fork ring longer when its handle is pressed against a wooden table?
How does a pressure cooker finish a pot of beans sooner than an ordinary pot with a loose lid?
